/**
 * Minimal leveled logger with colored output.
 *
 * All messages are written to stderr via `console.error`, regardless of level.
 * This is intentional: in Node.js, `console.info` and `console.debug` write to
 * stdout, which would interleave log lines with the stdout of the command
 * wrapped by awf and break callers that parse or pipe that output.
 */
class Logger {
args.command: grep -q '/\*\*' src/logger.ts && grep -q 'class Logger' src/logger.ts && grep -q 'All messages are written to stderr' src/logger.ts && echo "PASS" || (echo "FAIL" && exit 1)

#!/bin/sh
# Verify that src/logger.ts has JSDoc and documents the stderr rationale
if grep -q '/\*\*' src/logger.ts && \
   grep -q 'class Logger' src/logger.ts && \
   grep -q 'All messages are written to stderr' src/logger.ts; then
  echo "PASS: JSDoc and stderr rationale are present"
  exit 0
else
  echo "FAIL: Missing JSDoc or stderr rationale in src/logger.ts"
  exit 1
fi
